mutant.description: SEVEN controls. (1) THE UNFILTERED LOG CONTROL beside every filtered count, in all three windows, per this seat's own row D2-S51. (2) THE WORKSPACE SEARCH RE-RUN UNLIMITED after a head limit returned exactly its own limit. (3) THE EVENTBRIDGE COUNT taken client-side after auto-pagination, because a server-side filter plus length() reports per page. (4) THE DECISIVE EQUALITY TEST: lastLogin == updatedAt, which identifies the writing statement rather than merely describing it. (5) THE CALL-SITE POSITION of that statement computed against the three status guards, rather than assumed. (6) THE TOOL'S OWN WRITES enumerated from its code to see whether any sets updatedAt. (7) The two history settings READ rather than assumed.
mutant.expected: (1) non-zero controls. (2) a true total above the limit. (3) one total, not page counts. (4) equal or unequal, decisively. (5) guards before or after. (6) sets or does not set. (7) whatever they read.
mutant.observed: (1) 108, 72 and 40 unfiltered events, so the three zeros for a disabled-account refusal are real absences. (2) a limit of 60 returned exactly 60 -- a page -- and unlimited returned 100. (3) THE CONTROL CAUGHT ITSELF: --query length(Rules) printed 100 and then 56, which are PAGE counts, and the server-side contains() filter ran per page too, so a matching rule on page 2 could have been dropped silently; counting client-side over the auto-paginated 156 with no NextToken gives a sound zero. (4) EQUAL, exactly. (5) the only real call site is auth.ts:204 and the guard at 106 precedes it, so a disabled row cannot reach the write. (6) all three ui-walk writes set armedBy/armedAt, passwordHash and status, and NONE sets updatedAt. (7) stream null, PITR ENABLED -- and I had written DISABLED from assumption before reading it, which the read corrected.

determinism.method: Every figure is a count, a name, a path:line citation or a timestamp comparison taken from a file on disk, one row read, two table descriptions, or a metric and log count with its window stated in epoch milliseconds. Nothing was invoked and nothing was written, so a repeat read of the same instant's data must agree with itself.
determinism.observed: The counts reproduce. ONE ASSUMPTION OF MINE WAS WRITTEN BEFORE IT WAS READ and then corrected: I recorded point-in-time recovery as DISABLED while building the file, then read describe-continuous-backups and found it ENABLED. The correction matters rather than being cosmetic, because PITR being enabled means the row's prior STATES are recoverable in principle -- the single most informative read still available on this question -- while still not naming an actor. The file now carries the measured value, says plainly that I had assumed the other, and records the restore as forbidden by this order and not performed.

declared_exclusions.reason: NOT RUN, as the order forbids. `status` was run ONCE, which it permits, and reads status=disabled, armed=no, armedBy=none -- so an arm/disarm cycle had completed and the lease was returned. Nothing was enabled.

NOT PERFORMED, and the order forbids restoring. PITR is ENABLED, so a restore to just before each write would show WHICH ATTRIBUTES changed -- which my projections cannot -- but it would still not name the caller, since PITR records state rather than actors. Named as an available but unused instrument so the next seat knows the option and its limit.

declared_exclusions.item: Which client authenticated inside an armed window
declared_exclusions.reason: NOT ESTABLISHED, and this is the honest limit of the verdict. The row carries no actor field; a successful session was minted while the row was active, and by construction the walk password lives only in SSM and is read in-process by the walker. A sign-in log line naming the client, or the SSM parameter's access record, would close it. The log lines were COUNTED and never printed, so no actor was extracted from them.
